title.en: Hard-surface bevel geometry and normal contract

summary: Design bevels for visible highlight width, constrain overlap, and decide whether exported geometry normals or destination recomputation owns hard-surface shading.
objective: Rounded highlights survive glTF import without self-intersections, melted large faces, or accidental shading changes when Three.js displays the evaluated mesh.
applies_when: A manufactured, architectural, or environment asset needs finite edge radii and stable large-face shading.
example_prompts: Prepare a beveled appliance enclosure whose large panels stay visually flat in Three.js.
Set a reusable edge-radius policy for a modular sci-fi corridor kit.
negative_signals: Use normal smoothing to fake a silhouette-changing radius
Add segments without checking delivered triangles
not_for: Tangent-space normal-map interpretation, which belongs to the rendering handoff.

principles: A bevel serves two visible jobs: it changes silhouette at sufficient scale and creates a highlight transition. Width is an object-space design quantity; segment count is a sampling choice.
Topology and normals are separate decisions. Hardened or weighted normals can stabilize broad faces, but they cannot repair overlapping bevel geometry or replace an edge radius visible in silhouette.

Choose one normal owner. Export approved split normals when art-directed shading matters; recompute in Three.js only under a documented crease policy and accept that it is a different asset interpretation.
implementation: Apply object scale before judging an absolute bevel width. Group edge widths by physical role, such as casing, panel and micro-edge, rather than assigning arbitrary values per object.

Use the minimum segments that make the grazing highlight and target silhouette acceptable at the closest camera. Enable Clamp Overlap or reduce width where concave features collide; inspect the resulting geometry rather than relying on the toggle alone.
For hardened-normal shading, create the custom split-normal data required by the modifier and use Face Strength with a Weighted Normal workflow when that is the chosen large-face policy.
Export the evaluated mesh with normals. In Three.js, retain imported normals and let the material/light setup reveal them; do not silently call a recompute step during load.
Build a test coupon containing an outer corner, concave notch, narrow slot and large planar panel. Review wireframe, face normals and a moving grazing light.
observable_checks: The coupon has no intersecting or collapsed bevel faces at the narrow slot and concave notch.
A grazing light produces continuous edge bands while the large panel remains visually planar.
Imported vertex/triangle counts and normals are stable across repeated exports with the same settings; a deliberate normal recomputation yields a detectable comparison difference.

creative_affordances: Exaggerate a hero object's radius for readable highlights while keeping background props simpler.
Use deliberately faceted bevels for a stylized machined look when silhouette review approves them.
known_limits: The correct radius and segment count depend on scale, camera distance and lighting.
This record does not define normal-map tangent conventions.
Authored reusable guidance; no export, import or runtime artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender's Bevel modifier exposes width and segment controls, Clamp Overlap limits width to avoid overlapping intersections, and Harden Normals adjusts bevel-face vertex normals to match surrounding faces while requiring a custom split normals attribute; Face Strength can be used with a Weighted Normal modifier.
claims.scope: Documented Blender 4.5 Bevel modifier controls; the source does not select artistic values or promise a particular renderer result.

source_refs.locator: Width; Segments; Clamp Overlap; Harden Normals; Face Strength
